title: A retirement home in San Vitaliano (Naples) gave expired drugs to the elderly.
text: San Vitaliano is a comune (municipality) in the Metropolitan City of Naples in the Italian region Campania, located about 25 km (16 mi) northeast of Naples. San Vitaliano borders the following municipalities: Marigliano, Nola, Saviano, Scisciano.

title: The Filadelfia Stadium in Turin was reopened.
text: The Stadio Filadelfia, originally known as Campo Torino is a small multi-use stadium in Turin, Italy, situated in Borgo Filadelfia in the Lingotto district. Designed by the former President of Foot-Ball Club Torino, Count Enrico Marone Cinzano, the ground was opened in 1926 and continuously hosted all of Torino's home games until 1958.

title: After 15 years in Serie A, Genoa were relegated to Serie B.
text: Genoa Cricket and Football Club is an Italian professional football club based in Genoa, Liguria. The team competes in Serie A, the top division of the Italian football league system.

title: Rome was put on red alert zone for swine fever spread because of boars.
text: Classical swine fever or hog cholera (also sometimes called pig plague based on the German word Schweinepest) is a highly contagious disease of swine (Old World and New World pigs). It has been mentioned as a potential bioweapon.

title: In the town of Brusciano (Naples), 17 representatives were arrested from groups linked to Camorra.
text: Brusciano is a municipality in the Metropolitan City of Naples, in Italy, on the slopes of Mount Vesuvius. Situated inland north-east of Naples, 10 miles from center city, the ancient village of rural vocation has developed along the way National Puglia, in the stretch that connects the east of the capital and Pomigliano d'Arco and Nola.

title: Monkeypox arrived in Italy.
text: Mpox, originally known as monkeypox, is an infectious viral disease that can occur in humans and other animals. Symptoms include a rash that forms blisters and then crusts over, as well as fever and swollen lymph nodes.

title: Milan won Serie A after 11 years.
text: Associazione Calcio Milan, commonly referred to as simply Milan (Italian pronunciation: ) in Italy or AC Milan outside of Italy, is an Italian professional football club based in Milan, Lombardy. Founded in 1899, the club competes in Serie A, the top tier of Italian football.

title: Salernitana became the first team not to be relegated to Serie B with 31 points.
text: Unione Sportiva Salernitana 1919 is an Italian professional football club based in Salerno, Campania. The original club was founded in 1919 and has been reconstituted three times in the course of its history, most recently in 2011.

title: The 30-year anniversary of the Capaci massacre, where the anti-Mafia judge Giovanni Falcone was killed, was commemorated.
text: The Capaci bombing was a terror attack by the Sicilian Mafia that took place on 23 May 1992 on the A29 motorway, close to the junction of Capaci, Sicily. It killed magistrate Giovanni Falcone, his wife Francesca Morvillo, and three police escort agents, Vito Schifani, Rocco Dicillo and Antonio Montinaro; agents Paolo Capuzza, Angelo Corbo, Gaspare Bravo and Giuseppe Costanza survived.

title: First hospitalization for monkeypox in Arezzo.
text: Arezzo is a city and comune (municipality) and the capital of the province of the same name in the region of Tuscany in Italy. Arezzo is about 80 kilometres (50 miles) southeast of Florence at an elevation of 296 metres (971 ft) above sea level.

title: A shooting took place in the comune of Qualiano (Naples).
text: Qualiano is a comune in the Metropolitan City of Naples in the Italian region Campania, located about 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) northwest of Naples. Qualiano borders the following municipalities: Calvizzano, Giugliano in Campania, Villaricca.

title: In a school in Bergamo, a cylinder exploded and 5 children were burned.
text: Bergamo is a city in the region of Lombardy in northern Italy. The seat of the province of Bergamo, it is located approximately 40 km (25 mi) northeast of Milan, and about 30 km (19 mi) from the alpine lakes Como and Iseo and 70 km (43 mi) from Garda and Maggiore.

title: After the Caserta pride parade, homophobic graffiti and attacks were recorded.
text: Caserta is the capital of the province of Caserta in the Campania region of Italy. An important agricultural, commercial, and industrial comune and city, Caserta is located 36 kilometres north of Naples on the edge of the Campanian plain at the foot of the Campanian Subapennine mountain range.

title: 2022 Marmolada serac collapse.
text: On 3 July 2022, a serac collapsed on the mountain of Marmolada, in the Dolomites at the regional border between Trentino and Veneto, Italy. Eleven people were killed and eight were wounded.

title: 3–6 July – Olympics of the Real Neapolitan pizza were held.
text: Neapolitan pizza is the version of the round pizza typically prepared in the Italian city of Naples and characterised by a soft, thin dough with high edges. The tomatoes are traditionally either San Marzano tomatoes or pomodorini del Piennolo del Vesuvio, which grow on the volcanic plains to the south of Mount Vesuvius, and the cheese is traditionally mozzarella di bufala campana or fior di latte di Agerola.

title: Teramo Calcio and Campobasso Calcio were excluded from the 2022–23 Serie C season.
text: Campobasso Football Club, commonly referred to as Campobasso, is an Italian football club located in Campobasso, Molise, currently playing in Serie C, the third tier of Italian football. The club traces its roots back to 1919 and plays its home games in the Stadio Antonio Molinari, the largest outdoor stadium in Molise and one of the largest in Southern Italy, with a capacity of 21,800.

title: The first convictions for the attacks on the CGIL headquarters in autumn were issued; all Forza Nuova participants were sentenced to six years in prison, except the two leaders, who were placed under house arrest.
text: The Italian General Confederation of Labour is a national trade union centre in Italy. It was formed by an agreement between socialists, communists, and Christian democrats in the "Pact of Rome" of June 1944.

title: The Catania football club was re-founded and would restart from Serie D.
text: The Serie Dˈdi]) is the highest level of semi-professional football in Italy, and the fourth tier of the Italian national league system, the lowest one with a national organization. It sits beneath the third and lowest fully professional league, Serie C, and feeds in to it through promotion and relegation.

title: The 2022 Italian government crisis of the Draghi government began.
text: The 2022 Italian government crisis was a political event in Italy that began on 14 July. It includes the events that followed the announcement of Giuseppe Conte, leader of the Five Star Movement and former Prime Minister of Italy, that the M5S would withdraw its support to the national unity government of Mario Draghi over a bill regarding an economic stimulus to combat the ongoing energy and economic crisis.

title: The West Nile virus returned to Italy, with the first cases in Veneto and Emilia-Romagna, and one death registered.
text: West Nile virus is a single-stranded RNA virus that causes West Nile fever. It is a member of the family Flaviviridae, from the genus Orthoflavivirus, which also contains the Zika virus, dengue virus, and yellow fever virus.

title: Domino's Pizza announced that it would pull out of the Italian market after seven years.
text: Domino's Pizza, Inc., trading as Domino's, is an American multinational pizza restaurant chain founded in 1960. The corporation is Delaware-domiciled and headquartered at the Domino's Farms office park in Ann Arbor Township near Ann Arbor, Michigan.

title: The investigation into the 1996 disappearance of Angela Celentano was reopened.
text: Angela Celentano is an Italian missing person. Her disappearance occurred on 10 August 1996 on Monte Faito in the municipality of Castellammare di Stabia, in the province of Naples.

title: Brothers of Italy caused controversy after criticizing the cartoon Peppa Pig for including a lesbian couple.
text: Peppa Pig is a British preschool animated children's television series created by Neville Astley and Mark Baker. Produced by Hasbro Entertainment and Karrot Animation and formerly Astley Baker Davies, the series follows Peppa, an anthropomorphic piglet, and her family and friends portrayed as other animals.

title: 15–16 September – The 2022 Marche flood occurred.
text: The 2022–23 European windstorm season was the deadliest and costliest European windstorm season on record, mainly because of the impact in northern Libya of Storm Daniel, which became the deadliest and costliest medicane ever recorded as well as the deadliest tropical or subtropical system worldwide since 2013. The 2022–23 season was the eighth instance of the European windstorm naming in Europe.

title: The 2022 Italian general election took place.
text: Early general elections were held in Italy on 25 September 2022. After the fall of the Draghi government, which led to a parliamentary impasse, President Sergio Mattarella dissolved Parliament on 21 July, and called for new elections.

title: Ignazio La Russa became president of the Senate of the Republic. He was the first politician with a neo-fascist background to hold the position of President of the Senate, the second highest-ranking office of the Italian Republic.
text: Ignazio Benito Maria La Russa is an Italian politician who is serving as president of the Senate of the Republic since 13 October 2022. He is the first politician with a neo-fascist background to hold the position of President of the Senate, the second highest-ranking office of the Italian Republic.

title: Ultraconservative Lorenzo Fontana became president of the Chamber of Deputies.
text: Lorenzo Fontana is an Italian politician and member of the League (Lega), who is serving as President of the Chamber of Deputies since 14 October 2022. Fontana served as Minister of European Affairs in the Conte I Cabinet.

title: Volleyball player Paola Egonu decided to leave the Italian national team after various racist insults.
text: Paola Ogechi Egonu is an Italian professional volleyball player. She plays as an opposite for both the Italian Women's National Team, and the Italian Club, Vero Volley Milano in the A1 division of the Lega Volley Femminile.

title: In Naples, the NAS closed the pizzeria that invented the pizza Margherita (in 1889) due to poor cleaning.
text: A pizzeria is a commercial establishment specializing in the preparation and sale of pizza. It may offer take-away, where the customer orders their food either in advance or at the restaurant and then takes the prepared food with them in a pizza box.

title: The Salerno police and the financial police arrested a drug dealer for selling drugs on the seafront.
text: The illegal drug trade is the global black market dedicated to the cultivation, manufacture, distribution, and sale of prohibited drugs. The terms drug trafficking and narcotrafficking are also commonly used to describe the trade of the illicit substances.

title: Giorgia Meloni received the task of forming a new government from President Sergio Mattarella; she became the first female prime minister in Italian history.
text: Giorgia Meloni is an Italian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Italy since October 2022. She is the first and only woman to hold the office and the head of the longest-serving government in the history of the Italian Republic.

title: Six people were put under house arrest after stealing fish from Salerno markets.
text: House arrest is a legal measure where a person is required to remain at their residence under supervision, typically as an alternative to imprisonment. The person is confined by the authorities to their residence.

title: The Meloni Cabinet became operational. It was variously described as a shift to the political right, as well as the first far-right-led coalition in Italy since World War II.
text: The Meloni government is the 68th and current government of the Italian Republic, the first headed by Giorgia Meloni, leader of Brothers of Italy, who is also the first woman to hold the office of Prime Minister of Italy. The government was sworn in on 22 October 2022.

title: A man stabbed five people, including the Monza Calcio player Pablo Marì in the city of Assago (Milan).
text: Associazione Calcio Monza, commonly referred to as Monza, is a professional football club based in Monza, Lombardy, Italy. The team plays in Serie A, the top tier of Italian football, following promotion from Serie B in the 2025–26 season.

title: The 100th anniversary of the March on Rome.
text: The March on Rome was an organized mass demonstration in October 1922 which resulted in Benito Mussolini's National Fascist Party (Partito Nazionale Fascista, PNF) ascending to power in the Kingdom of Italy. In late October 1922, Fascist Party leaders planned a march on Rome.

title: Thousands of supporters of Benito Mussolini paraded.
text: Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini was an Italian fascist politician who served as the prime minister of Italy from 1922 until his deposition in 1943. Known as Il Duce during his regime, he established a totalitarian dictatorship led by the National Fascist Party (PNF) in the Kingdom of Italy.

title: Italy was officially a candidate to host Euro 2032.
text: The 2032 UEFA European Football Championship, commonly referred to as UEFA Euro 2032 or simply Euro 2032, will be the 19th UEFA European Championship, the quadrennial international football championship organised by UEFA for the senior men's national teams of its member associations. Italy and Turkey will host the tournament, which is expected to take place between June and July 2032.

title: 2022 Ischia landslide.
text: Heavy rain hit the island of Ischia, located in the Tyrrhenian Sea, causing damage to the comune of Casamicciola Terme. Twelve people were killed and five others were injured.

title: In the Denise Pipitone case, former prosecutor Maria Angioni was arrested for making false claims about the investigation to find the girl who disappeared 18 years earlier.
text: Denise Pipitone is a missing Italian girl who disappeared on September 1, 2004, while she was near the house of her maternal grandmother in Mazara del Vallo.
